item.title: Redis Interview Notes
item.description:
Sorted Sets (ZSET)

A sorted set maps each unique member to a score and orders members by score. Range queries and updates are typically O(log N).

Compact Encoding

Small sorted sets can use a compact listpack representation. Redis converts to its general representation when the set exceeds limits such as zset-max-listpack-entries or zset-max-listpack-value. Older Redis versions used a ziplist and correspondingly named settings. Check the settings for the version you run.

item.title: Redis High Availability
item.description:
References: Redis replication, Sentinel, and Redis Cluster.

Primary–Replica Replication

Replication provides copies of data and can serve reads from replicas. A primary accepts writes and sends updates to its replicas. Replication is asynchronous, so a replica can lag behind a successful write.

Full Synchronization

  1. A replica connects to a primary and requests synchronization with PSYNC.
  2. If a partial sync is impossible, the primary responds with FULLRESYNC, including its replication ID and offset.
  3. The primary produces an RDB snapshot and sends it to the replica while buffering subsequent writes.
  4. The replica loads the snapshot and applies the buffered updates, then continues receiving the replication stream over a long-lived connection.

To configure a replica, use REPLICAOF <primary-host> <primary-port>. A full sync consumes network and CPU resources; replicas can also replicate from other replicas to reduce load on the primary.

item.title: Redis Caching Patterns and Failure Modes
item.description:
References: Redis query caching, caching patterns, and Redis key eviction.

Caching Patterns

Cache-Aside (Lazy Loading)

On a read, the application checks Redis first. A hit returns immediately. On a miss, it queries the database, stores the result in Redis, and returns it. The cache is filled only for requested data, which suits read-heavy workloads and keeps the cache smaller.

Read-Through

The application asks a cache provider for data. The provider performs a database read on a miss and manages filling the cache, so the application does not contain the miss-handling logic.
